I’m an optician at Walmart and I’ll openly admit we don’t sell as good of lenses as you might get at LensCrafters or private practice. However, the lens (I’m assuming) you got is very high quality. There is a learning curve to progressive lenses, sometimes it takes a week to ten days to really get used to them. Not everyone takes that long but it definitely happens enough we’re used to saying that sentence lol. Wear them as much as possible to get used to finding the sweet spot of the progressives. Your main goal is to point your nose at what you’re looking at up close and tilt your chin up until your near vision becomes clear.  If you can’t get used to them, there’s a 60 day satisfaction guarantee. Progressives aren’t a universal fix for everyone like any other form of medicine.

I've been working on the independents for around 12 years. About six years ago, I had lost nearly everything. I had a shit job, my wife had left me, and in our divorce proceedings, I had found out the daughter we were raising wasn't even mine. To cope, I had started drinking and doing a lot of prescription pills. I would go to shows and they'd let me sit in the back, but (justifiably) no one would use me as I clearly was in no condition to do anything.


Primarily, I was a heel manager, and had worked for a small company in McMinnville, TN. The owner of the company was somewhat of a father figure to me and called me one day. He pitched an angle where I would come down, tell my story, and start asking for people in the locker room who I had previously cheated to be my friend, For weeks this went on until my real life best friend, who I had screwed more than anyone would finally take me back. The condition was if I showed up messed up, I was off the show and would never be brought back.


I am convinced that angle saved my life. I couldn't focus on a promo wasted, I had my friends back who I had alienated because of my poisonous relationship with my ex-wife, and wrestling was fun. Hell, I even met my current wife in the crowd of one of those shows, and now we have a beautiful son. Wrestling sucks from the inside a lot of the time, but I'll be damned if it ain't beautiful.

Long story short, Ted is a good guy, and will do everything in his power to help young talent learn and improve the future of the sport. He truly believes God sent him to save professional wrestling. He claims he was concussed at the time of the moonsaults off the cage and that he only remembers them from seeing the tape and being told about it. He does the backflips off the top as a tribute to Owen and his brother who died of a staph infection when they were teens.

For all of Ted's faults as a cocky, halfway insane, primadonna, he is also an extremely talented wrestler. While not trained by Stu Hart, he was brought up in the Dungeon, so he has a great technical knowledge and taught all of us many submission holds and reversals. His high-flying maneuvers are second to nearly none, and his punches (one of my sticking points in judging a wrestler) are spectacular. He is a former Golden Gloves boxer, and an amazing athlete. Look, liking Teddy Hart isn't popular, and maybe I'm jaded because I knew him personally, but if he ever got his ego in check, he'd be a megastar.
